edges.effect_quant: In the 20-year Gruppo Italiano cohort of 1213 patients with polycythemia vera, 634 major thrombotic events occurred and stroke was classified among the major events; in a multicenter recurrent-thrombosis cohort, 191 of 494 first thrombotic events were cerebrovascular and recurrent thrombosis occurred in 33.6% of patients overall.
edges.population: adults with polycythemia vera in hospital-based and population-based cohorts
edges.mechanism: Polycythemia vera raises hematocrit and blood viscosity while also promoting platelet, leukocyte, and endothelial activation. That combination increases arterial thrombosis risk, and cerebral vessels are one of the classic territories where this hypercoagulable, hyperviscous state can present.
edges.summary: Polycythemia vera is a well-established thrombotic disorder, and stroke is one of its classic arterial complications. Across long-term cohorts, cerebrovascular events appear both as presenting events and as recurrent complications during follow-up.
edges.caveats: Many studies report arterial thrombosis composites rather than stroke alone, so the precise stroke-specific absolute risk varies by cohort, age, treatment intensity, and prior thrombosis history. Modern therapy lowers risk, but it does not eliminate it.
